result.headline: Terrain blocking the line to every nearby mast is the likely cause [terrain_blocking].
result.explanation: Terrain blocking is the most likely cause: 466 people are in cells where hills block the line to every site within 5 km [zone_overview], and new high-ground masts would give clear lines to most poorly served people [cand_1][cand_2][cand_3]. Distance is also likely: 1,140 people have no identified site within 5 km, while existing sites are 3.2–5.7 km away [zone_overview][existing_1][existing_2][existing_3]. Operator identities for two sites are unknown, so coverage per operator is not confirmed [existing_2][existing_3]. A single-operator gap is not proven because existing sites list EE, Three and Vodafone [existing_1], even though only 0.5 operators on average have approximate sites within 5 km [zone_overview]. The evidence cannot separate terrain from distance or operator-specific gaps because only 5 Ookla tests with low data confidence exist [zone_overview][fix_rule]. Mast heights are assumed, so the margin is uncertain [terrain_blocking]. Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level. best_network: EE, Three and Vodafone are listed at existing site S002028 [existing_1]; S002029 and S000928 operators are unknown [existing_2][existing_3]. No site identified in our data for other operators. Confidence low because evidence is weak. Actions for a resident: try the best network; Wi-Fi calling indoors; check the address on Ofcom's mobile coverage checker (https://www.ofcom.org.uk/mobile-coverage-checker); emergency calls work on any available network.
